To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immunosuppressive drug regimen based on mTOR inhibitors and calcineurine inhibitors (CNIs) is associated with a significant decrease of total and LDL cholesterol, and a significant increase of HDL cholesterol, and that the mTOR inhibitor everolimus has a significant beneficial effect on lipid profile in patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection.
the mTOR- and CN- based immunosuppressive regimens are associated with a different metabolic profile in adult patients after LT.

the mTOR- and the calcineurin-inhibitor-based immunosuppression regimen is characterized by different metabolic changes, with the mTOR-based regimen being associated with an increased risk of metabolic syndrome and the calcineulnrin-based immunosopression with an increased risk for hypertriglyceridemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of immunosuppressive therapy on lipid metabolism, and in particular, on the effects of mTOR and calcineurine inhibitors.
the study of the effects of mTOR- and CN-based immunosuppression in lipid and carbohydrate homeostasis in patients undergoing liver transplantation.
the development of new methods for the analysis of the dynamics of biological systems, and their application to the study of the immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) tacrolimus (TAC) is not associated with any significant increase in the risk of developing new-onset diabetes mellitus (NODM) in liver transplant patients compared to the use of cyclosporine (CY).
the use of calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) in the long-term immunosuppression of liver transplant patients is not associated with a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular disease.
the use of the calcineurin-inhibitor-based immunosuppression regimen is not superior to the mTOR-inhibitor-based regimen in terms of metabolic changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the molecular mechanism of how the immune system regulates the metabolism of lipids and carbohydrates.
the mTOR and calcineurine-based immunosuppression regimen has a significant influence on lipid and carbohydrate metabolism in liver transplant recipients.

the use of the mTOR inhibitor everolimus in addition to the calcineurin inhibitor cyclosporine (CsA) in liver transplantation is associated with an improvement in the metabolic profile, especially with a decrease in the incidence of new-onset diabetes after liver transplantation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mTOR inhibitor sirolimus is superior to the calcineurin inhibitor cyclosporine in terms of lipid profile and carbohydrate metabolism in adult patients undergoing liver transplantation.
the calcineurin inhibitors, cyclosporine and tacrolimus, are not the only drugs that can cause kidney damage in transplant patients.
the mTORC1 pathway is important for regulating lipid metabolism and the mTORC2 pathway is important for controlling carbohydrate metabolism.
